originalProposal:
When Peter preached Christ, the crowd was pierced to the heart and asked what they should do. Peter called them to repent and be baptized. Acts tells us that those who received his word were baptized, and about three thousand souls were added that day. The gospel came first, followed by a real response of faith and obedience. These were not anonymous spectators who simply attended an event; the Lord was gathering a people.

This helps us understand why I teach salvation and believers' baptism as the pattern of belonging to the church. We are saved by Jesus Christ, not by signing a church membership card. Baptism is the believer's public act of obedience and identification with Christ. I teach immersion because it vividly pictures our burial with Christ and our rising to walk in newness of life. Acts 2:41 gives the order of receiving the word, being baptized, and being added; it does not describe the exact procedure for every baptism or prescribe a modern membership system.

The people added that day continued together in teaching, fellowship, prayer, and shared life. When we join a local body, we are identifying ourselves with fellow believers whom we intend to love, serve, encourage, and be accountable to. Membership should express that living commitment, never become a substitute for knowing Christ.
